title: Whether white trumpet players played like Black players
summary: Punch says white players at first sounded mechanical but later picked up bending notes and growls from Chicago arrangers.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did the white trumpet players play about the same as the colored? Yeah.

Not way back, but now lately they are. On them way back there years ago, they couldn't get it, you know. For some reason they couldn't get it, but by them guys, you know, writing, like in Chicago anyway, them guys like Dave Payton, Fletcher Henderson, them guys used to write stuff for them boys, see. And they started getting that up. They couldn't read the music. Oh, they want to get that text, you know, that right text. Well, they made it so mechanical. Yeah, that's what I'm talking about. You can't feel it, see. That's right. That's what I'm talking about. Yes.
But I wondered, would they bend notes and stuff like that most times? Would they use a growl or anything, the white trumpet players like that?

That's what I'm telling you now, all that come to them. There wasn't at the beginning. Yeah. But all that come to them, man. Everything. It really come to them. Like Winging Alone and Primo. Boy, them boys would start out playing us a straight home, but they got together, they got all that stuff together like everybody else, you know.
